Chapter 6: The Long Road to Healing
Stepping out from the shadows of a life where every move was controlled by someone else, that first taste of freedom... it’s a wild mix of excitement and confusion, isn’t it? Suddenly, the world outside the FLDS feels enormous. There’s noise everywhere, and choices—so many choices—each one a little reminder of everything that used to be off-limits.
For anyone who’s managed to escape, the journey to healing isn’t a straight line. Honestly, it feels more like learning to walk all over again after years of being told you had to sit still. Even the smallest decisions—like picking out cereal in a grocery store—can feel huge. Imagine standing in the aisle, staring at all those boxes, and realizing you’ve never really chosen for yourself before. That freedom is a gift, sure, but it can also be overwhelming. And those old rules? They stick around, whispering doubts and warnings when you least expect it.
There are bright moments, too. Buying a colorful dress just because it makes you happy. Laughing with brand-new friends. Tasting food you never thought you’d ever try. Each one is a little celebration. But then, there are nights when the past comes crashing back—memories of harsh words, punishments, and that constant fear of slipping up. Healing, it turns out, isn’t about erasing those memories. It’s about learning how to live with them and, bit by bit, finding a way to move forward.
Therapy ends up being a lifeline. Sitting across from someone who just listens—no judgment, no agenda—can be incredibly powerful. The process is slow, and there are days when it feels like you’re not getting anywhere. But with every session, the heavy weight of shame and guilt starts to lift. You come to realize your feelings are valid, your pain is real, and you’re not the only one going through this.
Reaching out to others who’ve left the FLDS brings a whole new sense of belonging. In small support groups, stories get shared—stories about loss, survival, and hope. There’s real comfort in knowing you’re not alone, that everyone’s journey is hard, but it’s also possible. Together, you celebrate the little wins: landing a new job, finding a safe place to call home, or just having the courage to speak up for yourself.
Of course, the outside world isn’t always kind. Not everyone gets what it’s like to leave a closed community. Some people are just curious, others can be downright judgmental. There are awkward questions, and it’s easy to feel isolated. But over time, you start to trust yourself more. You discover strengths you never even knew you had—resilience, compassion, and this fierce determination to create a better life.
Healing isn’t about wiping away the past. It’s about reclaiming your future. And with every step, you get a little closer to a life that’s truly yours—built on your own choices, fueled by your dreams, and grounded in your own sense of self-worth.
